title: Fog
description: Looking straight up between the Canary Wharf towers into a summer cumulus sky, with air that knows how far away everything is. Drag up or scroll to shorten the visibility, down to clear it; the haze gathers a little thicker wherever the pointer rests. The far towers go first, turning the blue of the sky they stand in, the cumulus fade behind the veil while their edges stay crisp, and the glass corner overhead stays sharp in front of it all.
intent: Aerial perspective, after Makoto Shinkai's skyward city shots and the worm's-eye summer photographs herb loves: converging towers, a cobalt zenith, cumulus. Beer-Lambert transmittance per pixel and per channel (Rayleigh-leaning, blue extinguished first) through a haze layer that thins with height, along a metric distance converted from a Depth Anything V2 map. Drag sets the meteorological visibility (Koschmieder, beta = 3.912 / V) from 50 km to 150 m, mapped so the visible change runs evenly along the gesture: log V spends the clear-day kilometres, which change nothing in a 400 m frame, in the first tenth of the drag, so the far tower is already turning by fog 0.1 (~2 km), past half blue by 0.2 (~1.1 km), four fifths blue by 0.35 (~600 m) and a cobalt silhouette with the low sky veiled by 0.5 (~330 m). The extinction is depth-separated, in layers along the street: the haze lies out down the street, so what a tower's ray crosses is set by its horizontal distance (d cos e, not the slant distance, which Depth Anything ramps out along a face that recedes upward). The street around the viewer is swept clear to about 30 m, the canyon's own air (2.3 times the open column's) fills in over the next 30 m and holds, and past about 150 m, where the street opens toward the docks, a bank of haze (3.2 times) thickens over 100 m; each is a density ramp crossed in closed form, slanted by 1 / cos e and thinned with height (scale 120 m, so a ray that climbs to a tower's crown leaves some of the street's haze under it, while the crowns far up a receding face still haze before its base). So the middle of the drag is a ladder of blue values: at fog 0.4 the glass corner and the right tower overhead keep over 95% of their light with their black point, the right slab tower and the Canada Square block about three fifths and a half, visibly blue-shifted but keeping their floors, and the back-right slab and the far tower an eighth and a twenty-fifth, a cobalt silhouette. The slab, a tower under construction far down the street on the right, had been merged by Depth Anything into the right tower in front of it; its distance is put back behind it (tools/depth/bakes/fog/slab.py) along the right tower's straight edge, so the two layers part. At fog 0.8 the far layer is gone and the mid towers are down to a tenth or a fifth while the glass corner keeps over 90%: it never takes the far towers' tint. Only the last stretch of the drag, the arrival's field of haze, closes the clear pocket and takes the near glass. The in-scattered light comes from the sky itself. In front of a tower it is the open sky at that tower's own elevation, measured off the plate between the clouds (#5a9fcc low, deepening toward #2f7fb8), with extinction per channel and no lift toward white, and in front of a tower it leans halfway from the horizon haze toward that open blue (the canyon's air is lit from overhead), so a far tower fades to a cobalt silhouette on the cobalt behind it, never to milk, and it keeps its build: the haze is a transmittance, not a veil laid over the towers. Each tower's light mixes toward the air's by fogAmt = 1 - T along its distance, so the crowns far up a receding face haze first and the bases stay crisper, and the air's light is multiplied by the tower's own light against its local mean (its pixels alone, blurred a little wider than its floors), so a window or a shadowed bay a fifth of its neighbours' light takes a fifth of the air's too. Darks scale toward the sky's blue instead of lifting to it: a fogged tower is a sky-tinted version of itself, faint cobalt on cobalt with its floors and mullions inked, never a flat slab or a milky ghost, and the canyon's air sits well under the sky's (0.62 of it), so the towers stay worm's-eye silhouettes against it. The haze is one medium along every line of sight, the sky and its cumulus included: a ray to a tower crosses the air out to that tower's distance, a ray past them crosses the haze column by airmass (1 / sin of its elevation, floored at 0.15) times the haze's density, and both take on the same in-scattered light at their elevation. Low down the street that light is the cyan of horizon haze on a summer day (#8FB8D4), so the low sky and the gaps between the low cumulus lift a little and lose some of their saturation toward it, staying cyan rather than going to milk (about #95C0DB, s 0.5, at fog 0.7, where the clear plate is an electric s 0.86), easing higher up into the sky's own light, so the zenith stays deep cobalt and the sky deepens toward it. In front of a tower that light is a little dimmer (the canyon's air sees less of the sky), so a tower the haze has taken sits just under the sky behind it, never a lighter slab: its air light is held under 0.8 of the hazed sky or cloud luminance beside its silhouette, cloud shadow included. The air is also lit by the sun, which haze scatters forward: a Henyey-Greenstein lobe (g 0.6) toward the capture's sun, just past the top edge of the frame, warm-white (#FFF1E2) over the cumulus and in the sky's own colour over the open blue (warm-white over cobalt reads lilac), weighted by the air's opacity, so the clouds toward the sun stay cream under the haze while the low sky down the street, looking away from it, keeps its cyan. Clear air keeps its blacks: on a solid still clearly seen the shadows are taken down to the print's black point (the glass's deepest reflections under about 35 of 255 at fog 0.7), easing out with the transmittance, and the film's diffusion spreads into the darks at under a third of its strength, so the near glass corner is the sharp, inked anchor the haze recedes from. Distance and sky matte are snapped to the silhouettes (Depth Anything pulls a tower's edge toward the sky's distance for tens of pixels; each edge band takes its tower's interior distance instead), so the haze stops exactly where each tower does; the matte the air reads is coverage, not a switch: along each silhouette a guided filter on the plate's own colour softens the snapped matte onto the plate's edge, and every edge pixel blends the tower's distance and air with the sky's by how much of it is sky, so the silhouettes keep their sub-pixel shape at any size instead of stair-stepping. The far tower's roofline, where a reflection in the crown and the railing posts had bitten the matte, is closed and rebuilt with the same guided filter, so its top edge is clean. The haze in front of the sky only veils it, keeping all of the cumulus' local detail (the plate less its blur at the scale of the cloud's forms) so the low cloud reads as cloud through the air, never airbrushed: forward-scatter softening touches the towers, never the clouds. The plate is two Poly Haven HDRIs (CC0, from their 16k captures) rendered at 3840 through the same stereographic rays: canary_wharf for the towers, docklands_01 for the sky, its cumulus unmixed from the capture's own blue and laid back over a radial cobalt (pale #2081AC where the sky meets the towers, #044984 in the middle of the opening) premultiplied by that same cover, so nothing of the capture's sky is left as a pale ring round each cloud and the edges thin into the new cobalt as they did into the old. The clouds are then lit again rather than ranked by luminance: across a thickness proxy (the cover blurred at the scale of a cumulus' lobes) the light runs from skylight-blue shade (#93B1CB) on the thin margins to cream #FFF1E2 on the thick bodies, never a grey, leaned toward the sun just past the top edge (each cloud's own shadow, its cover marched toward the sun, and a broad gradient toward it) and toward the capture's own lit lobes, with a terminator as wide as a lobe, so no hard cream crescent is laid along any rim. The ladder gives the hue and stops short of the shoulder in luminance, and the capture's own folds (its band-pass light, less its blur at about 12 px of a 2560 frame, steepened where the shoulder flattens the brightest bodies) ride on it at full strength over the whole interior, easing in only over the outermost few pixels of each silhouette, so every cloud has the capture's texture throughout and reads as a lit volume with crisp folds, not an airbrushed blob with a sticker top. The mid-thickness dips inside a thick body, where the unmixed cover let the cobalt through as blotchy holes, are floored to 0.9 of the cloud-scale cover and take the light of the cloud round them, and no cloud pixel prints darker than the cobalt under it, so the margins carry no dark flecks. After the haze a split grade takes only what the air laid over a cloud, on the luminance the haze left and weighted by how much of that light is the sun's, so a veiled cumulus top still lands on the warm end instead of the air's cyan and a clear one keeps its own light. A film finish runs last: a diffusion bloom, a filmic shoulder whose top is warm (above about 0.9 in luminance the light rolls off toward cream #FFF1E2, never neutral paper-white), glass graded away from the sky's blue, a thin amber halation under the highlight edges (the sunlit cumulus and glints only, never the pale cyan sky against a tower), and 24 fps grain at scan scale held for two frames.
